evidence: A green candidate served the marker and both fixture items received passing judge scores; the run passed and recorded the eleven specified effects in order, including gate-attempt-passed.
After R-1 failed at the fence, a second start of R-1 for C-2 was refused run-already-started; the run list held only R-1 for C-1.
While R-1 was running its sleeping builder, R-2 was refused run-in-progress; progress showed R-1 running and R-2 absent.
After R-1 passed, R-2 for the same cycle was refused cycle-already-run, and R-2 progress was null.
Started R-1 with a nonexistent deadbeef commit; start-run refused not-a-commit, and run-progress returned null. No builder host was invoked.
An empty plan produced a refused checklist with empty-checklist and halted before the self-check or fence.
A plan containing an unstamped scenario recorded its stamp, then halted at stamp because the identities differed, with no pin or checklist.

A self-check printing golden checklist differs failed the cycle at the fence for harness-self-check-failed, but the recorded detail included a trailing newline and a fail-cycle effect followed the self-check, contrary to the stated last-effect Then.
The passing self-check printed SKIP bb-tools; its recorded harness-self-check-passed event listed bb-tools.
Fencing an absent path refused fenced-path-matched-nothing, then recorded fail-cycle and failed at fence for fence-refused without a builder.
The builder observed one root commit and one commit, with fenced paths absent from the object graph; the non-fenced gitlink retained mode 160000 and the cut’s identical object ID.
A red first candidate and green repair launched two builder sessions with distinct identities; regenerate completed before the first gate and subsequent repair launch.
The builder left a green candidate and exited 1; regenerate recorded its digest and the run passed.
An empty successful builder launch produced no regenerate effect; fail-cycle recorded candidate-not-regenerated and the cycle failed at regenerate.
A builder sleeping for 30 seconds under a two-second regenerate budget was stopped; the cycle failed at regenerate for budget.
A server already answered the configured port; three gate refusals each produced gate-refusal, then the cycle failed for infrastructure and the launch sentinel was absent.
The red suite recorded suite-red, never launched start.sh, and exhausted the one gate attempt.
A candidate without start.sh recorded a gate-attempt-failed event for contract-missing.
A green suite served a page without the configured marker; with one allowed attempt the gate recorded identity-probe-failed.
The builder changed its test.sh to fail after exit; the gate’s copy retained the passing test, the gate passed, and install and regenerate digests matched.
The repair builder saw the clean room, previous candidate and gate evidence; attempted writes to the latter two were denied. Its repair event named the first gate’s evidence root.
Three red candidates caused three builder launches and three failed gates; the cycle failed for gate-attempts-exhausted, without a verdict-file effect or researcher requests.
The common researcher code failed for 01-002 and scored 01-001; file-verdicts held only 01-001, and measurement filed 01-002 unreached with 1 of 2 passing.
R-1 failed at fence and R-2 halted at checklist; after five seconds both retained their statuses and identical effect results.
Two reads of the passed run returned identical progress.
The probe accepted only one URL argument at the configured port and verified the marker; the gate and run passed.
The candidate suite created and removed a directory under its own scope; the gate passed and install and regenerate digests matched.
The passing self-check printed the legacy SKIP line; its recorded event listed the entire text after SKIP.

With stdio selected and no port, the green suite, probe and store check passed; the gate event recorded 30 seconds, one poll answered on 1, and answered as the context, and the cycle passed without a refusal.
The probe received the absolute gate-room start.sh and 30, with GATE_STORE outside the gate room and no LOYLY_ variables; the store check received the same path.
A red stdio suite recorded suite-red; its environment had neither GATE_STORE nor LOYLY_ variables, and neither probe nor store check ran.
The failing stdio probe produced identity-probe-failed with its boot-budget message; the store check did not run.
A passing probe and failing store check produced identity-probe-failed with the store-check message, exhausting the one attempt.
The stdio suite checked for the plan spec beside it in its working tree; the gate passed and the install and regenerate digests matched.
An absent stdio store-check command halted the run at gate for effect-could-not-run, without a gate result.
Two stdio runs with different store-check command texts recorded passing self-checks with different harness digests.
A symlinked plan slice stamped and derived 01-001 and 01-002 with sources under plan/01-a; the run continued and failed at the empty builder rather than halting.
With PLAN_SLICES=02, only slice 02 was stamped and the checklist contained only 02-001.
Both builder launches received the configured image as the third argument; regenerate and repair details named the image and the same digest.
A configured missing builder image caused builder-image-missing; run-progress returned null and no builder was launched.
Two runs passed on one store; C-2’s scoreboard named C-1 as previous, and its stamp recorded no new identity.
A probe read its marker beside itself at harness/config.sh and checked the served page; the gate passed and regenerate and install digests matched.

The command gate ran once in the project repository with an empty candidate scope in the gate tree, a separately copied candidate matching the install digest, and an empty evidence directory. Its pass recorded BOOT 20 10, ANSWERED 3 and ledger answered as itself; the command did not launch the candidate.
The first gate command returned suite-red with detail 3 of 65 tests failed; the repair saw its proof file read-only, and the second gate passed.
The gate command returned seam-answered-before-boot three times; each refusal was followed by gate-refusal, and the cycle failed at gate for infrastructure.
The gate command returned an unrecognized infrastructure line; progress halted at gate with effect-could-not-run and that detail, without a gate result, fail-cycle or cycle.
Three passing runs with no gate command, gate-a and gate-b had three distinct harness digests. The first matched the SHA-256 of configuration bytes, self-check command text and probe bytes in order.
The green HTTP run passed and recorded the eleven expected effects. Grain’s reference event-store check confirmed each effect result lies in its named leaf of the run or a delegated child.
A server rejected its first three requests and the gate passed on poll 5 with a 20-poll budget. The run’s cycle progress attempt did not show the required boot-margin-polls of 15.

A red first candidate and green repair passed on attempt 2. Grain shows two gate-attempt.v1 child ticks with each attempt’s install, self-check and gate in its own tick, and repair in the first; the reference event-store check confirmed named-leaf containment.
A copy of the candidate under a temporary directory with no .pi ancestor ran the green HTTP fixture; attempt 1 and the cycle passed. The temporary copy was removed after profiling.

The two judges scored 01-001 pass/booked and 01-002 fail/no receipt; measurement filed 1 of 2 and the run passed. The store profile shows two distinct grade.v1 child traces of the run and two judge score events.
The researcher returned E-ONE for 01-001 and E-TWO for 01-002. The first judge request held E-ONE, while the second researcher and judge requests did not.
The researcher request carried the scenario, seam and event model; its shell reported Linux, the item grading room and only that room under its parent, with clean-room files and candidate copy.
The judge returned a reason for 01-001 and no reasoning for 01-002. Progress and the store showed one judge score, and measurement filed 01-002 unreached with 1 of 2 passing.

Started a run with approval r-1 and a different rubric-derived SHA-256 digest; progress halted at grader with refused-before-the-cycle and named the actual digest. Its effects stopped at checklist, with no self-check, fence, or builder launch.
The researcher model returned HTTP 400 for both items. File-verdicts was refused zero-verdicts, fail-score-stage was recorded, and the cycle failed at score without another builder launch.

The runner and sleeping builder were stopped five seconds into the first session; restarting on the same store resumed and passed. Both builder launches carried the same session identity, and stamp, pin, checklist, first self-check, fence and regenerate each appeared once.
The builder recorded exactly INSTRUCTION-7 on its first launch; the repair instruction added only a closing paragraph naming the previous candidate and gate evidence paths.
A model stub returned HTTP 400 for render; progress halted at render for effect-could-not-run, with no regenerate or fail-cycle effect and no cycle. The builder host was not launched.
While the builder slept, progress showed R-1 running with a tick identity, completed fence and render nodes, and regenerate marked running.
